--- title: "[Graph.hub_centrality()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Get HITS hub scores for each node (directed graphs only). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L30729-L30876){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.hub_centrality( max_iter=100, tol=1e-06, attr_name=None, return_dict=False, ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![HITS hub scores](/assets/graphs/hub-centrality.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="The same five-node directed graph shaded by hub score. A points to B, C and the top authority D and scores 0.82; B and C each point to D and score 0.41; D and E point to no authority and score 0." width="100%"} HITS (Hyperlink-Induced Topic Search) computes authority and hub scores for nodes in a directed graph. Hub score measures how much a node points to good authorities: `hub(v) = sum of authority scores of nodes v points to` and, in turn, a node is a good authority if good hubs point to it (see `authority_centrality()`). The two scores are defined in terms of each other, so they are computed together by power iteration: starting from all-ones vectors, each round recomputes hubs from the current authority scores and authorities from the current hub scores, then rescales both vectors to unit Euclidean length. The process stops when neither vector changes by more than `tol=` between rounds, or after `max_iter=` rounds. Hub scores identify nodes that are valuable as *pointers* to important content: - review articles or surveys that cite the key papers in a field - directory and portal pages on the web - curators, aggregators, or brokers in follower and trade networks Unlike out-degree, which counts every outgoing edge equally, a high hub score requires pointing to nodes that are themselves widely endorsed. Edge weights are ignored. The graph must be directed. Each iteration scans all edges once per node, so the method is best suited to small and medium-sized graphs. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[100]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of power-iteration rounds. Defaults to `100`. If the scores have not converged by then, the values from the last round are returned without a warning, so increase this for large graphs or when `tol=` is very small. Very small values (such as `1` or `2`) give rough approximations dominated by out-degree. [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence threshold. Iteration stops once the sum of absolute changes between two consecutive rounds is below `tol=` for both the hub and the authority vector. Defaults to `1e-6`. Larger values stop earlier with less precise scores. [attr_name]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Column name used to store the scores in the node DataFrame. If `None` (default), the column is named `"hub_centrality"`. An existing column with the same name is overwritten. Only used when `return_dict=` is `False`. [return_dict]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[False]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True`, return the scores as a dictionary and leave the node DataFrame untouched. If `False` (default), store the scores under `attr_name=` and return the graph for method chaining. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Union[dict[int, float], Graph]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `return_dict=` is `True`: dictionary mapping node IDs to hub scores. The scores are non-negative and normalized so that their squares sum to `1`. If `return_dict=` is `False` (default): returns self for method chaining. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If graph is undirected. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} In this small citation network, "Paper1" cites both other papers. The roles are the reverse of `authority_centrality()`: "Paper1" is the only hub and takes the whole score, while the cited papers, which cite nothing, score `0`: ::: {#422660ea .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["Paper1", "Paper2", "Paper3"]) .add_edges( [ ("Paper1", "Paper2"), # Paper1 cites Paper2 ("Paper1", "Paper3"), # Paper1 cites Paper3 ] ) ) scores = graph.hub_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in scores.items()} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {'Paper1': 1.0, 'Paper3': 0.0, 'Paper2': 0.0} ``` ::: ::: In a slightly larger graph, A points to B, C, and D; B and C also point to D; and D points to E. A is the best hub because it points to every authority, including the top one, D. D has an outgoing edge too, but its only target, E, is not an authority, so D's hub score converges to `0`: ::: {#51f398df .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D", "E"]) .add_edges([("A", "B"), ("A", "C"), ("A", "D"), ("B", "D"), ("C", "D"), ("D", "E")]) ) scores = graph.hub_centrality(return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(scores.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` {'A': 0.816, 'B': 0.408, 'C': 0.408, 'D': 0.0, 'E': 0.0} ``` ::: ::: Capping the iterations with `max_iter=` shows the scores before convergence: after two rounds D still holds a noticeable hub score, because early authority scores are essentially in-degrees and E does have an incoming edge: ::: {#89c9d1ca .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} rough = graph.hub_centrality(max_iter=2, return_dict=True) {graph.get_label_from_id(nid): round(s, 3) for nid, s in sorted(rough.items())} ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {'A': 0.754, 'B': 0.452, 'C': 0.452, 'D': 0.151, 'E': 0.0} ``` ::: ::: With `return_dict=False` (the default) the scores are stored in the node DataFrame and the graph is returned, ready for further chaining: ::: {#1c662e34 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} ( graph .hub_centrality(attr_name="hub") .get_node_df() .select(["label", "hub"]) ) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}
